clue.text: Animal painter working to capture extremely comic duck

indicators.note: to capture means the painter-plus-working pair holds the other letters inside

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is the crossword's standard painter
on means working, as a machine that is on

indicators.note: extremely asks for the word's first and last letters only

parts.note: a duck is a nought in cricket, so the letter O

explanation.surface: An artist at work on a wildlife picture includes a comically drawn duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal painter' reads as one phrase, a wildlife artist, but only 'Animal' defines; 'to capture' signals the container round the comic letters and duck.
explanation.definitionFit: A raccoon is a ringtailed North American mammal, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Old policeman done by con man, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a Bow Street ..., an early London police officer
to flee without paying, as a swindler might

explanation.definitionFit: Bow Street Runners were early police, and doing a runner means absconding.

clue.text: One who painted cattle on a wreck

indicators.note: wreck tells us to smash up the letters of cattle on a and rebuild them

explanation.surface: An artist depicts cattle aboard a shipwreck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wreck' rearranges CATTLE ON A.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaletto was the Venetian painter famed for views of Venice, so one who painted.

clue.text: He killed two foes, losing head about others

indicators.note: about means the shortened foes goes round the other piece
losing head means the first letter of foes goes

parts.note: the rest are the others

explanation.surface: A warrior despatches a pair of enemies, then beheads one among others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He killed two' is the definition; 'losing head' beheads the foes and 'about' wraps them round the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Orestes killed both his mother Clytemnestra and her lover Aegisthus in Greek myth.

clue.text: Beak's protector is acquainted with rest, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals words spoken that sound like the entry

parts.note: acquainted with is knows, and rest is peace

explanation.surface: A magistrate's bodyguard is familiar with taking a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' only joins; KNOWS PEACE, spoken, gives the answer. Beak is slang for nose (and for a magistrate).
explanation.definitionFit: A nosepiece on a helmet guards the nose, which slang calls the beak.

clue.text: Get rich, disposing of duke's second ring

indicators.note: disposing of means getting rid of a letter from the duke's name

parts.note: Prospero is the rightful Duke of Milan in Shakespeare's The Tempest
a ring is the round letter O; second picks the later of the duke's two Os

explanation.surface: Someone makes money by selling off a nobleman's spare ring.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the final O of PROSPERO, Shakespeare's magician duke, leaves the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is to thrive financially, a synonym of growing rich.

clue.text: Grass, creating general alarm

definitions.meaning: a kind of millet-like grass of the genus Panicum

explanation.definitionFit: Panic grass is a millet-type grass, and panic is sudden widespread fear.

clue.text: Old American tyrant goes in for taxing

indicators.note: goes in means the tyrant is put inside the other letters

parts.note: US means American
Nero was the tyrannical Roman emperor

explanation.surface: An ex-US despot enters politics to raise taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes in' is the container signal; 'taxing' looks like a tax verb but means burdensome.
explanation.definitionFit: Onerous means burdensome, the sense of taxing as demanding.

clue.text: Zoroastrian's son raised in capital city

indicators.note: raised in means the letter for son is lifted higher up the capital, this being a down clue

parts.note: Paris is the French capital

explanation.surface: A Parsee's boy grows up in the big city.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, raising S moves it up one place in PARIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsis are Indian followers of the Zoroastrian religion; the def's 's is a contraction of is.

clue.text: Advance across river and adopt country ways

indicators.note: across means the advance word spans the river

parts.note: to rise is to advance or move up
the Ural is a river of Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: Someone presses on over a river and settles into rural life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' is the container signal; 'and' only joins. 'Advance' as a noun misleads: it is the verb meaning go up.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruralise is to take on country life and manners.

clue.text: Nobody has news about reformed snooper

indicators.note: about means the news letters go round the rest

parts.note: news is read as a plural of new, N twice

indicators.note: reformed means the letters of snooper are made over in a new order

explanation.surface: A gossip magazine reports that a former spy has gone straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' is the anagram signal and 'about' the container; reading news as two N letters is an unusual convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonperson is someone treated as having no existence or importance, a nobody.

clue.text: Slip over in bar or restaurant

indicators.note: over means the run of letters is read backwards
in signals letters sitting inside the words bar or restaurant

explanation.surface: Someone takes a tumble in a pub or a café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds RORRE within 'baR OR REstaurant'; 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small mistake, the same as a mistake made in passing.

clue.text: Dine with most of class in Israeli port

indicators.note: in means the shortened class goes inside the word for dining

parts.note: to dine is to eat

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: ilk means kind or class

explanation.surface: A traveller has a meal with classmates at a harbour in Israel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops a last letter and 'in' is the container signal; 'with' only joins the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Eilat is Israel's port on the Red Sea, at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba.

clue.text: Magazine chosen before recess, say

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken, giving a word of like sound

parts.note: chosen is picked, and before it a recess, an oriel window, follows

explanation.surface: A periodical is picked before the parliamentary break.
explanation.walkthrough: PICKED + ORIEL, spoken, sounds like the answer; an oriel is a projecting bay window, hence a recess.
explanation.definitionFit: A pictorial is a periodical full of pictures, an illustrated magazine.

clue.text: Tacky quality of stone slab in army quarters

indicators.note: in means the slab sits within the army and its quarters

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, the British reserve force
the quarters are compass points: S, S, N, E, S, S
a stele is an upright inscribed stone slab

explanation.surface: A garish monument has been put up in a barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the slab within the army and its quarters, here the compass points south, south, north, east, south, south.
explanation.definitionFit: Tastelessness is vulgarity, the quality of being tacky.

clue.text: Acquit person involved in old charge

indicators.note: involved in means the person sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: ex means former or old
a rate is a charge
one means a person

explanation.surface: Clear someone who was caught up in a former accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' is the container signal; a charge here is a price, not an accusation.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to clear of blame, to acquit.

clue.text: Indispensable as oil might be

explanation.definitionFit: Essential means vital, and an essential oil carries a plant's essence.

clue.text: Two blokes supporting broadcast rock

indicators.note: supporting means the blokes come under the broadcast in a down entry

parts.note: OB is an outside broadcast
Sid is a man's name
Ian is a second man's name

explanation.surface: A couple of men are backing a programme about stone.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, supporting means coming below: SID IAN under OB.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsidian is a black volcanic glass, a kind of igneous rock.

clue.text: Capability I displayed on piste, oddly bringing credit?

parts.note: Capability Brown was the great English landscape gardener

indicators.note: oddly means the letters of on piste appear in a strange order

explanation.surface: A skilled skier shows off on the slopes in the hope of praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' turns ON PISTE into EPOINTS; 'displayed' only joins. Capability Brown was an 18th-century English garden designer.
explanation.definitionFit: Brownie points are notional credit earned for doing something approved.

clue.text: Strange thing that is worn by some retired people

indicators.note: strange tells us the letters of thing are jumbled

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: An odd garment is worn by some pensioners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' turns THING into NIGHT; retired means gone to bed, not stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightie is a nightdress, something worn by people who have gone to bed.

clue.text: Downfall of Geordie area, one in chaotic state

parts.note: Geordies come from Newcastle in the North East of England

indicators.note: in means one goes inside the chaotic state

parts.note: a mess is a chaotic state
I is the Roman one

explanation.surface: A northern region collapses into disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts I inside MESS. A Geordie is a person from Newcastle upon Tyne, in North East England.
explanation.definitionFit: A nemesis is an agent of ruin, someone's downfall.

clue.text: Family man's first tool for correcting type

indicators.note: first means the man comes before the family

parts.note: bod is slang for a man or person
kin are family

explanation.surface: A father's chief implement is for editing print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts BOD ahead of KIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodkin is a pointed tool printers used to pick out type for correction.

clue.text: Combine to get note accepted by unappreciative type

indicators.note: accepted by means the note is taken inside the other word

parts.note: an ingrate is an ungrateful person
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Teamwork needs a message welcomed even by an ungrateful colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted by' is the container signal; 'to get' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To integrate is to combine parts into a whole.

clue.text: Farmer half-heartedly becomes doorkeeper at lodge

indicators.note: half-heartedly means half of the double letter at the heart is removed

parts.note: a tiller tills the soil

explanation.surface: A reluctant farmer becomes a gatekeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' drops one of the two central Ls of TILLER.
explanation.definitionFit: In Freemasonry the tyler or tiler guards the door of the lodge.

clue.text: Trial involving a southern state

parts.note: to say is to state

explanation.surface: A court case involving a state in the South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: An assay is a test or trial, especially of metal purity.

clue.text: Fruit no good for a Communist chairman to eat

indicators.note: to eat means the chairman takes the other letters inside

parts.note: Chairman Mao led Communist China

explanation.surface: Some produce is judged unfit for a Communist leader's table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eat' puts N G inside MAO.
explanation.definitionFit: A mango is a tropical stone fruit.

clue.text: One of Langerhans's detached territories?

parts.note: the ... of Langerhans are cell clusters in the pancreas, read jokily as small detached lands

explanation.definitionFit: An islet is a little island, a detached territory, and the pancreas has the islets of Langerhans.

clue.text: Stay with friends backing knockabout comedy

indicators.note: backing means the word for friends is read in reverse

parts.note: pals are friends
to stick is to stay put

explanation.surface: Someone sticks around with mates who support a broad comedy act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns PALS into SLAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapstick is boisterous physical comedy, the knockabout kind.

clue.text: An area of cultivation, this creche?

definitions.meaning: a place where young plants are raised
a room or place for looking after small children

explanation.definitionFit: A nursery is both a plant-raising ground and a place where young children are cared for.

clue.text: Greek character's quiet store in centre of Birkenhead

indicators.note: in means quiet and store go inside the central letters
centre of takes the middle letters of Birkenhead

parts.note: p is piano, quiet in music
a silo is a store for grain

explanation.surface: A Greek man's peaceful shop sits in the middle of a Merseyside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' takes the town's two middle letters and 'in' is the container signal. Birkenhead is a town on Merseyside.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth letter of the Greek alphabet.
